measurement_contract.notes: Runtime-shape measurements are the internal notebook parity closure payload. They must report wall time, CPU time, peak RSS, Numba thread count, maximum Python process fan-out, stage_b_execution_mode, stage_b_process_fallback_threshold, and exact_replay_count.

authority_layers.notes: Synthetic perf-smoke validates the committed benchmark contract, deterministic serialization, and gate semantics, but it does not grant final corrective closure by itself.

Final corrective closure for canonical notebook-parity scenarios requires explicit live benchmark measurement on the benchmark host. Missing live_host_captures keep closure open even when synthetic contract validation passes.

equal_thread_budget_rule.notes: Compare backend and notebook only when host, artifact slot, and numba_threads_used all match exactly. Accepted benchmark thread budget currently freezes max_numba_threads=4 with stage_a_workers=4 and stage_b_workers=1 for the canonical exact_parallel backend shape. Closure accepts only the single-process default and finalist-only exact replay runtime shape when sync and worker backend measurements are reviewed together with stage_b_execution_mode and stage_b_process_fallback_threshold.

acceptance_gates.notes: Backend end-to-end runtime must stay within 1.18x of the notebook runtime on the equal thread budget.
Backend peak_rss_bytes must stay within 1.35x of the notebook peak RSS on the equal thread budget.
NR2 must remain single-process by default on the benchmark-sized path.
NR2 should resolve in the no-risk terminal path instead of generic Stage B.
No-risk runs must not cross any non-default Stage B process workload threshold.

scenarios.notes: NR2 is the canonical no-risk two-indicator parity class. The committed comparison points show the current backend-vs-notebook gap and keep both 4-thread and 12-thread notebook references reviewable.

baseline_reference_points.notes: Current benchmark-host default keeps RG-TTR Stage B in-process, so the canonical parity shape stays in one Python process unless a non-default profile explicitly enables process fan-out.
The canonical RG-TTR notebook anchor is a single-process multi-thread exact shape and provides the comparison point for process fan-out and stage_b_execution_mode.

acceptance_gates.notes: RG-TTR backend runtime must stay within 1.18x of the notebook runtime on the equal thread budget.
Benchmark-sized RG-TTR workloads must not fan out into multiple Python worker processes by default.
Benchmark-sized RG-TTR workloads should keep Stage B in-process by default.
Benchmark-sized RG-TTR workloads must stay below the non-default process fallback workload threshold.
RG-TTR breadth scoring must keep the fast Stage B path active so exact_replay_count stays within the finalist-only replay bound after the in-process default cutover.

scenarios.notes: RG-TTR is the canonical risk-grid parity class. The committed backend default now records the single-process default in-process Stage B shape plus finalist-only exact replay so future regressions fail on unexpected worker amplification or replay breadth drift.

baseline_reference_points.notes: RG-ALT is functional-first in the first wave. Runtime may not regress by more than 10% against the committed backend baseline on the same host and equal thread budget.

acceptance_gates.notes: RG-ALT keeps functional coverage only in the first wave, but runtime must not regress by more than 10% against the backend baseline.

scenarios.notes: RG-ALT keeps the alternative ranking metrics reviewable without claiming notebook parity in the first wave. Measurements must still emit the full runtime-shape payload, including stage_b_execution_mode, stage_b_process_fallback_threshold, and exact_replay_count.
